executiveSummary: State-linked threat activity against OT is ongoing. U.S. agencies report Iranian-affiliated actors actively compromising PLCs across Government Services, Water/Wastewater, and Energy, including manipulation of project files and alarms. Immediate removal of internet exposure and logic integrity validation are directed. Security Advisory CISA separately urged the Water/Wastewater sector to protect internet-exposed PLCs after observed password changes and IP reconfiguration caused boil-water notices and manual operations. Security Advisory Supply-chain and perimeter management exposures remain high-risk: actively exploited TeamCity RCE and N-able N-central auth bypass were added to CISA's KEV Catalog, enabling CI/CD takeover and MSP-driven lateral movement into operators. CISA KEV CISA KEV Factory-implanted backdoors were found in multiple Zbtlink routers used at the edge; an unauthenticated root shell is exposed and beacons every ~35 seconds-high risk of OT pivot at remote/field sites. View Article Enterprise gateways remain a principal ingress: F5 BIG-IP APM and Ivanti EPMM unauthenticated RCEs show active exploitation and web-shell persistence. Organizations should isolate, patch, and perform compromise assessments before re-enrollment. CERT-FR Alert CERT-FR Alert Adversary use of covert router/IOT networks for staging and masking operations continues at scale (FSB Center 16; PRC "covert networks"), with strong recommendations to harden SNMP/SMI, disable TFTP/FTP, and replace EoL devices. items: Iran-affiliated operators: Active PLC intrusions with program/download abuse and HMI manipulation across multiple sectors. Security Advisory
Russia FSB Center 16: Router exploitation using SNMP defaults and Cisco Smart Install to steal configs via TFTP/FTP, enabling credential theft and pivoting. Security Advisory
Mirage Kitten (UNC1549): New backdoors and WebSocket tunnelers target telecom/government/aerospace with DLL hijacking and proxy-aware C2. View Article
Pro-Russia hacktivists: Opportunistic HMI/VNC exposure abuse causing loss-of-view/parameter manipulation; prioritize VNC elimination from internet per guidance. Security Advisory

descriptions: Initial access via exposed OT services and weak/absent auth; router/SNMP/SMI abuse; default credentials (ATT&CK: T1190, T1078, T1110).
Supply-chain compromise of CI/CD and npm packages leading to credential theft and artifact poisoning (T1195, T1552, T1555).
Web-shells and deserialization RCE on gateways/APM/CI; living-off-the-land via SQL xp_cmdshell, PowerShell/WinRM (T1505.003, T1059, T1210).
PLC program/download manipulation, alarm suppression, parameter changes; HMI/VNC abuse (ICS: T0843, T0851; Enterprise: T1021.005).
Covert tunneling and WSS/HTTPS C2; SOCKS proxies; residential proxy masking (T1090, T1572).

outlook72h: Complete emergency checks for internet-exposed PLCs and router/CPE at remote sites. If found: disconnect, validate configurations, and restore from clean backups. Patch TeamCity, N-central, F5 APM, Cisco FMC, Ivanti EPMM; remove public exposure; rotate keys/tokens; review logs for unauthorized admin actions and web-shells. Block Zbtlink backdoor infrastructure and inspect for /usr/sbin/kworker and related artifacts on listed models; plan device replacement. Audit CI/CD artifacts released in the last 30 days; rebuild/sign from trusted environments if TeamCity exposure is suspected. Deploy or tune OT protocol monitoring (CIP/S7/Modbus) to alert on downloads/mode changes and alarm suppression patterns.
